title: This / These - dies-
sourceNote: The transcript is garbled in several example sentences; the examples were reconstructed into standard German following the teacher's explanation of all cases and genders.
objectives: I can point at something with *dieser, diese, dieses*
I can use the correct ending of *dies-* for gender and case
I can use *dies-* after dative prepositions such as *zu* and *mit*
I can use *dies-* in the plural (diese, diesen)

expressions.en: I think this dress is nice.
How much does this sweater cost?

patterns.en: How much do these shoes cost?

grammar.title: dies- = this / these
grammar.body:
**dies-** points to a particular thing (this one here), maybe while you point at it with your finger. It works exactly like **welch-** in the last lesson: the endings are the endings of the definite article **der / die / das**.

Compare: **Ich finde das Kleid schön** (a dress we both know) and **Ich finde dieses Kleid schön** (this very dress, I am pointing at it).
grammar.ar: dies- تشير إلى شيء محدد (هذا). نهاياتها مثل نهايات أداة التعريف تمامًا.

examples.en: How much does this sweater cost?

grammar.title: Masculine: dieser / diesen / diesem
grammar.body: **der Pullover** → nominative **dieser Pullover**, accusative **diesen Pullover** (as object), dative **diesem Pullover** (after *zu*, *mit* ...).

examples.en: I think this sweater is nice.

grammar.title: Feminine: diese / diese / dieser
grammar.body: The feminine does not change between nominative and accusative: **diese Hose**. In the dative it becomes **dieser Hose**.

examples.en: I think these trousers are nice.

grammar.title: Neuter: dieses / dieses / diesem
grammar.body: The neuter does not change between nominative and accusative: **dieses Auto**. After *mit*, *zu* etc. it is **diesem Auto** (like masculine).

examples.en: I think this car is great.

grammar.title: Plural: diese / diese / diesen
grammar.body: In the plural the nominative and accusative are **diese**. In the dative it is **diesen**, and the noun gets an extra **-n** (unless it already ends in *-n*): **diesen Schuhen**, **diesen Kindern**.

examples.en: How much do these shoes cost?

grammar.title: Overview
grammar.body: Same endings as the definite article. Remember the dative plural noun gets **-n**.

tip: Use the same trick as with welch-: first find the case, then give dies- the same ending as the definite article.

comprehension.q: What does dieser / diese / dieses mean?
Which form do you use for 'this sweater' as an object?
What is the dative form of diese Hose?
What happens to the noun in the dative plural?

exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form of dies-.

items.q: Welches Kleid gefällt dir? - ___ Kleid. (Dieses / Diesem)
Welchen Pullover kaufst du? - ___ Pullover. (Dieser / Diesen)
Zu welcher Hose passt der Pullover? - Zu ___ Hose. (diese / dieser)
Mit welchen Kindern spielst du? - Mit ___ Kindern. (diese / diesen)

exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order.

items.a: Dieses Kleid gefällt mir. / Mir gefällt dieses Kleid.

items.q: How much does this sweater cost?
I think these shoes are nice.

summary: **dies-** means *this / these* and points at something specific.
Endings are the same as **der / die / das**: dieser, diesen, diesem; diese, diese, dieser; dieses, dieses, diesem; diese, diese, diesen.
Example sentences: **Ich finde diesen Pullover schön.** / **Was passt zu dieser Hose?**
